title: Senior Silicon Product Engineer – Manufacturing
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA’s Silicon Co-Design Group sits at the crossroads of architecture, silicon, systems, and manufacturing, where first-principles thinking and engineering judgment at the highest level translate directly into product outcomes at scale. Our team gets every GPU, SoC, and CPU silicon program from first power-on to high-volume production!


We are hiring a Senior Silicon Product Engineer – Manufacturing to join our Testability, Manufacturability, Reliability & Quality (TMRQ) team. In this role, you will co-design and implement SLT Production diagnostics for silicon features in a high-volume manufacturing environment, verify POR specifications, and support post-silicon validation for some of the industry’s most complex semiconductor chips. You should have experience defining and validating SLT production coverage specifications on silicon and translating product requirements into effective test coverage that delivers quality, yield, and efficiency at scale. Hands-on lab experience with system-level post-silicon bring-up and silicon debugging is required. This role sits at the intersection of multi-functional HW/SW teams and Production Operations to make manufacturing an outstanding part of the overall Silicon co-design cycle, production release, and HVM testing! The exceptional hire continuously improves high-volume manufacturing workflows and products multi-functionally and uses AI deliberately to drive impact while managing risk.


What you will be doing:

  • Partner multi-functionally with HW engineering teams such as Silicon PVT design and characterization teams, IO design and validation teams, system feature owners, SLT and BLT Production Operations, etc., to determine test coverage and constraints to resolve appropriate SLT test conditions, test content, and flows for high-volume manufacturing screens.
  • Partner with SW and platform teams to support and improve SLT testing infrastructure, debug knobs, and data collection features needed to support manufacturing screens effectively.
  • Co-design SLT testability scope and coverage enhancements for Nvidia's manufacturing testing with a focus on high-volume system-level manufacturing screens.
  • Prototype and fine-tune speed, power, circuits, yield, and quality for effective silicon coverage in the SLT socketed environment.
  • Co-design, develop, and maintain SLT testing flows and incorporate takeaways from silicon and correlate to design.
  • Define procedures to facilitate Silicon correlation activities between production testing infrastructure and internal Si characterization and diagnostics programs.
  • Support customer-facing and quality teams during customer escalations to understand the issues and fix gaps identified in SLT production coverage.
  • Drive alignment for manufacturability, test time optimization and reduction, cost vs. coverage tradeoffs, etc., to evaluate the effectiveness of new tests.
  • Initiate and drive process improvements and preventative actions through root cause analysis and data analytics.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree or equivalent in Microelectronics/Electrical/Electronic/Computer Engineering or equivalent experience.
  • 8+ years of relevant proven experience in silicon Post-silicon PVT validation and/or High-volume manufacturing testing for sophisticated SoCs, GPUs, CPUs, or similar.
  • Hands-on lab experience with silicon bring-up, lab debug, test content bring-up, and correlation to Si characterization, yield, and coverage optimization.
  • Strong EE fundamentals, device physics, knowledgeable in Silicon design, statistics, STA concepts, signal integrity, fault analysis, sampling, and computer architecture.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to drive multi-functional alignment around plans, dependencies, and sign-off criteria.
  • Prior ownership of manufacturing test strategy for a major silicon product (e.g., GPU/SoC/CPU) from early planning through ramp to QS/production.
  • Strong data analysis skills. Prior experience working with volume data is a plus.
  • Good understanding of firmware/driver structures and their interaction with HW.
  • Problem-solving, debugging, analysis, and logical reasoning skills with examples to prove it.
  • Experience with Python, BASH, Linux, and scripting.

Ways to stand out above the crowd:

  • Outstanding work ethic and up-leveling discussions to solve the real problems

title: Chip Level Defect Localization and Failure Analysis Engineer - RDSS Intern
descriptionHtml:
By submitting your resume, you’re expressing interest in our 2027 RDSS (Research and Development Substitute Services) program. Please confirm your eligibility with the local district office before applying for the role.


Welcome to the world of NVIDIA, where innovation knows no bounds. We've been at the forefront of technology for over two decades, and our groundbreaking invention of the GPU in 1999 revolutionized not only an industry but also the very way we engage with computers, robots, and autonomous vehicles. Today, NVIDIA stands at the forefront of AI computing and is committed to continue pushing the limits of what is achievable. Join us on this remarkable journey as we shape the future every day. Today, visual computing is becoming increasingly central to how people interact with technology, and there has never been a more exciting time to join our team!


We are looking for a skilled, creative, and highly motivated RDSS Intern in the field of Electrical Failure Analysis to join the electro-optical FA team in Hsinchu, TW.


What you'll be doing:

  • Your main job will be to perform electro-optical failure analysis including Photon-Emission, Laser-Voltage-Probing and Soft-Defect-Localization (aka SDL, LADA...) to support product development, design-debug, yield-ramp, reliability and customer return analysis of advanced flip chip devices manufactured in the most advanced CMOS technology.
  • The work requires in-depth understanding of scan-chain based logical test. Based on production test results (e.g. error-logs, flop mapping and SW-diagnosis) you will narrow down the logically failing area with the goal of locating the one failing FET or cell out of the whole chip.
  • Most analyses will require you to setup test-loops within our Advantest 93k tester SW. Additionally, you will use CAD layout tools for in-chip navigation and circuit simulation tools to aid your analysis. The goal is that our EFA results enable different Physical FA teams local and abroad to find the actual physical root-cause. Based on our work and the resulting PFA findings, our Foundry partners can improve their process technology and increase our product yield and reliability.
  • You will need basic Unix skills because the CAD, circuit simulation tools and 93k tester SW are all run in a Unix environment.
  • Design-debug and more complicated defect localizations will often require you working in multi-functional teams (e.g. with Design for Test, Test-Engineers and Product-Engineers, sometimes around the globe..) including presenting & explaining your results. To guide such team and PFA efforts you will need deep understanding of transistor physics, the CMOS fabrication processes and PFA tools/techniques such as SEM, TEM, FIB & AFM.
  • Support Die Probe Package second-source development for A16 FA readiness.

What we need to see:

  • Master's or PhD degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering or other related field
  • Basic understanding of DFT for large-scale logical test (scan-chain based structural and at-speed testing and basics of test compression).
  • Experience working in a lab, setting up and debugging test environments. / Functional knowledge of transistor device physics & advanced CMOS manufacturing processes. / Test bring-up in the Advantest 93k test environment.
  • Knowledge of CAD layout tools, logic circuit simulation tools and Unix operating system. / Software languages that may be of use include PERL, TCL, C++, STYLE.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills are critical.

title: Technical Lead - ADAS Test Bench
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is shaping the future of autonomous driving. Our Automotive Software team in Munich delivers cutting-edge autonomous driving solutions to leading global OEMs.


As the primary Plan of Record (POR) owner, customer interface, and technical escalation authority for the autonomous driving program, you will lead the technical specification, commissioning, and operational scaling of our open-loop bench farm. Having built, flashed, and debugged automotive test benches hands-on in your past engineering roles, you will now mentor and guide a dedicated cross-functional engineering team—including Technical Operations, Program Management, and Hardware Engineering—in diagnosing complex electronics, hardware, and signal integrity issues. Your mission is to scale our open-loop bench farm, automate bench workflows, and pave the way for expansion to future OEM platforms.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Define Bench Architecture & POR: Establish and own the technical Plan of Record for open-loop bench architectures, defining component BOMs, wiring schematics, power delivery, and sensor interfaces to achieve vehicle-equivalence.
  • Technical Mentorship & Escalation Leadership: Act as the top-level technical escalation point for on-ground Technical Operations engineers and technicians. Mentor the team in bringing up new benches, diagnosing component-level faults, and troubleshooting complex hardware issues.
  • Electronics & Hardware Troubleshooting: Guide hands-on diagnostics across ECU power supplies (12V external supplies, ground busbars), custom wiring harnesses (40-pin harness connectors, DB9 interfaces), console headers (UART-to-USB dongles for Orin/Aurix), and Aurix JTAG Lauterbach flashing headers.
  • Bus Communication & Sensor Integration: Troubleshoot and validate multi-sensor interfaces, including camera arrays, radar suites, Ultrasonic Sensor (USS) daisy chains, and Vector VN5620 CAN/CAN-FD replay interfaces.
  • Automate Bench Workflows & CI/CD Pipelines: Drive end-to-end automation of bench operational tasks, such as automated SoC and microcontroller firmware flashing, software deployment, remote logging, and integration of CI/CD test automation pipelines directly onto the benches.
  • Bench Farm Scaling & Capacity Planning: Lead the technical scaling of the Munich bench farm, standardizing bring-up checklists and qualification criteria so the architecture can scale to additional OEM programs.
  • Customer & Management Technical Interface: Represent bench technical readiness, operational status, and capacity roadmaps in technical syncs with software development leads, project management, and OEM client technical stakeholders.

What we need to see:

  • Education & Experience: Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field, combined with 8+ years of hands-on experience in automotive test bench operations (Open Loop / HIL), embedded hardware bring-up, and technical team leadership.
  • Hands-on Bench Engineering Background: Proven track record of personally building, wiring, flashing, and debugging automotive development benches from bare hardware to fully qualified setups.
  • Automotive ECU & Architecture Expertise: Deep domain knowledge of high-performance automotive ECU platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Orin, Infineon Aurix, Oak), custom vehicle harnesses, power distribution, and ECU pinout schematics.
  • Bus Protocols & Replay Hardware: Practical expertise in CAN, CAN-FD, Automotive Ethernet, gPTP time synchronization, and Vector diagnostic/replay interfaces (VN5620, CANoe/CANalyzer).
  • Electronics Diagnostics & Tooling: Advanced capability using oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, Lauterbach/JTAG debuggers, and ST Hub Debug units to isolate physical layer and signal integrity failures.
  • Automation & Scripting Skills: Proficiency in Python, Linux shell scripting, and build pipeline tools to automate bench commissioning, ECU flashing, and software validation workflows.
  • Leadership & Cross-Functional Communication: Excellent communication skills in English, with proven ability to mentor technical staff, manage customer interfaces, and coordinate across hardware, software, and program management.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Prior hands-on experience with NVIDIA DRIVE systems and reference setups.
  • Proven experience scaling lab or bench operations from small prototype groups to large multi-bench farms supporting production OEM programs.
  • Experience integrating multi-sensor replay setups (GMSL2 cameras, MateNet radars, USB/daisy-chained USS arrays) into automated software test pipelines.
  • German language proficiency.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Agent Policy Fabric
descriptionHtml:
The Agentic Safety Engineering team is building Agent Policy Fabric (APF), an enterprise governance layer for AI agents. APF combines signed policy, runtime verification, policy projection, credential mediation, and audit records to help govern the actions agents take across enterprise systems. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help turn the APF proof of concept into diligent production software. You will build, implement, test, and operate features in policy verification, runtime integration, or conformance testing. Working with experienced platform and security engineers, you will own a defined feature or subsystem and help ensure that policy decisions are accurate, integrations are reliable, and failures are handled safely!


Join us!


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build policy-verification features: Implement components of the Runtime Policy Verifier and authorization APIs, including signed policy validation, freshness and revocation checks, rollback protection, and binding decisions to the correct subject and runtime context, following reviewed security contracts.
  • Implement policy projection: Translate canonical APF policy into runtime-specific rules and adapter constraints. Handle unsupported policies and partial updates safely so runtimes admit work only when the required policy has been accepted.
  • Develop runtime integrations: Work with OpenShell and other runtime engineers to implement and test agreed interfaces for policy consumption, runtime context, admission decisions, and audit events. Document interface behavior and raise gaps or conflicting assumptions for resolution.
  • Strengthen correctness and conformance: Build fixtures, compatibility tests, negative tests, and property or fuzz tests that exercise policy behavior, integration boundaries, and failure paths. Investigate defects and turn findings into regression coverage.
  • Deliver production-ready components: Add observability, measure performance, debug reliability issues, and contribute to rollout plans and operational documentation for the components you own.
  • Contribute technical judgment: Write focused design documents, explain implementation tradeoffs, participate in code and security reviews, and work with platform, Identity, and Product Security partners to resolve issues within your scope.
  • Help the team deliver: Break work into achievable turning points, communicate dependencies and risks, review code, and share knowledge with other engineers.

What We Need To See:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, with 5+ years of relevant industry experience in systems software, backend services, distributed systems, security engineering, or policy infrastructure.
  • Strong programming skills in at least one of Rust, Go, C++, or Python, with experience delivering maintainable, tested production code.
  • Experience building and delivering services or systems components, including API design, integration, debugging, and error handling.
  • Practical experience implementing security controls, such as authorization checks, signature verification, or credential handling, and the ability to reason about trust boundaries and safe failure behavior.
  • Working knowledge of Linux, service-to-service interfaces, automated testing, CI, and software release workflows.
  • Ability to own engineering work through design, implementation, validation, and delivery; communicate technical tradeoffs clearly; and collaborate effectively through design and code reviews.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Experience with policy engines or authorization systems such as OPA/Rego, Cedar, Zanzibar-style systems, or runtime enforcement frameworks.
  • Experience with signed artifacts, trust-root distribution, key rotation, revocation, or tools such as Sigstore, TUF, or in-toto.
  • Familiarity with AI-agent runtimes, sandboxed execution, tool-call governance, MCP-style routing, or credential isolation.
  • Experience with protobuf/gRPC, schema evolution, backward-compatible APIs, or cloud and enterprise deployment environments.
  • Use of property testing, fuzzing, or other adversarial testing techniques to find security and correctness defects.

title: PhD Researcher Intern, World Foundation Models

title: Principal Engineer - Data Retrieval
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking an engineering lead to architect and scale the data acquisition infrastructure that powers our foundation models. Starting with code and STEM data for Nemotron, you will build the systems that discover valuable sources, crawl the open web at scale, and deliver reliable, high-quality data to training pipelines. This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning distributed systems, crawl infrastructure, and third-party data ingestion. You will own the architecture of a unified platform covering source discovery, URL indexing, crawl frontiers, predictive ranking, scheduling, distributed fetching, and ingestion. We have existing infrastructure to build on, and the goal is to bring it to pretraining scale and extend it to additional model families, modalities, and acquisition workflows over time. Along the way, you will lead architecture reviews and critical implementation work, mentor engineers, and help build the team.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Work with storage and scaling teams to design scalable frontier storage and queueing systems with high-throughput writes, efficient lookups, deduplication, and scheduling based on data quality, diversity, and freshness. Build a continuous discovery loop that extracts links and feeds new candidates back into the crawl frontier.
  • Develop a shared crawl execution layer that fetches reliably and politely at scale, handling dynamic websites while keeping resource use under control.
  • Build extensible pipelines for open-web, licensed, and partner content, including text, PDFs, code repositories, and multimodal assets. Define stable interfaces for source connectors so teams can add sources without rebuilding the platform.
  • Partner with parsing and curation teams to preserve valuable code, math, and structured content, and improve accepted data yield.
  • Implement provenance and policy enforcement with legal, privacy, security, and data governance partners. Translate approved publisher preferences, opt-outs, licensing terms, and use restrictions into auditable controls that follow the data downstream.
  • Own production readiness, including capacity planning, observability, fault tolerance, recovery, and cost efficiency. Instrument the pipeline end to end and set service objectives for throughput, freshness, reliability, and meeting training cutoffs.
  • Work with research and product teams to evaluate internal crawls and external datasets through comparable pilots. Deliver reproducible data releases that tie source coverage and processing quality to controlled training experiments.
  • Coordinate dependencies across teams and make clear tradeoffs between immediate data delivery and long-term platform development.

What we need to see:

  • A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • 15+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, including designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, setting technical direction, and delivering complex infrastructure across multiple teams.
  • Deep experience with web crawling or closely related discovery, indexing, or ingestion infrastructure, including distributed scheduling, stateful services, storage, and high-throughput data processing.
  • Strong hands-on engineering and system design skills. Ability to move between architecture, implementation, performance analysis, and production debugging.
  • Experience building batch or streaming pipelines and reasoning about consistency, retries, duplicate processing, backpressure, and recovery. A track record of improving throughput, latency, resource efficiency, or operational reliability.
  • Experience delivering data platforms for research, ML, search, or other demanding technical users. Ability to translate evolving requirements into clear interfaces and measurable engineering outcomes.
  • Strong technical communication and leadership through influence across engineering, product, research, and governance teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience architecting a web-wide crawl platform, scaling crawl frontier storage, or consolidating multiple acquisition systems into shared infrastructure.
  • Direct experience supplying foundation-model pretraining data, including targeted discovery, quality-aware crawl ranking, and acquisition of code or technical content.
  • Experience implementing publisher consent, training-use opt-outs, dataset licensing controls, or provenance infrastructure at scale.
  • Background with browser-based or agentic data collection, programmable extraction, and sandboxed environments for tool-use data or post-training evaluation.
  • Experience onboarding licensed or multimodal datasets, building reusable partner integrations, or delivering streaming feeds with low latency for retrieval and grounding.

The platform is a core capability for NVIDIA’s AI models and directly shapes the reach and quality of our training data. If you enjoy solving difficult distributed systems problems and building platforms that other teams depend on, we want to hear from you.

title: Senior Applied Research Scientist – Computational Geometry and Meshingmill
descriptionHtml:
Industrial simulation depends on turning product and device geometry into valid, efficient discretizations. This role will advance computational geometry, meshing, simulation-ready representations, and AI-native algorithms for NVIDIA GPU platforms.


We are looking for an applied researcher who can build methods that move design data reliably from CAD to simulation. You will develop geometry, meshing, and discretization algorithms that improve robustness, numerical accuracy, and end-to-end performance across CAE, EDA, semiconductor, and scientific-computing workflows. Join us in reinventing the geometric foundation of engineering simulation!


What you'll be doing:

  • Build algorithms for computational geometry, computer-aided engineering and design interoperability, mesh generation, mesh adaptation, spatial data structures, and curved discretization.
  • Investigate differentiable geometry, AI-native geometry processing, learning-based meshing and discretization, and design-to-simulation workflows for inverse design, simulation-ready digital twins, and autonomous engineering workflows.
  • Explore solver- and hardware-aware geometry and discretization methods that jointly optimize mesh quality, numerical accuracy, robustness, and comprehensive simulation efficiency.
  • Define benchmarks for mesh quality, geometry conversion, discretization accuracy, robustness, downstream solver impact, and end-to-end simulation performance.
  • Collaborate with teams across Omniverse, OpenUSD, Warp, solver engineering, NVIDIA Research, universities, and industrial partners involved in computer-aided engineering, electronic design automation, chip manufacturing, electronics, and digital twin workflows.

What we need to see:

  • PhD or equivalent experience in computer science, computational geometry, scientific computing, graphics, applied mathematics, computational mechanics, engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience.
  • Background in computational geometry, geometry processing, mesh generation, adaptive discretization, CAD and CAE algorithms, or simulation-ready representations with 5+ years proven experience working in computational engineering.
  • C++ and Python skills, with experience building algorithms for sophisticated geometry.
  • Understanding of boundary representations, topology, mesh quality, discretization error, numerical robustness, and solver requirements, supported by research, software, or industrial impact.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with CAD kernels or formats such as Parasolid, ACIS, Open Cascade, CATIA, NX, Creo, SOLIDWORKS, STEP, IGES, B-Rep, NURBS, or spline-based representations.
  • Experience with tetrahedral, hexahedral, polyhedral, anisotropic, adaptive, boundary-layer, curved, or high-order mesh generation.
  • Work in isogeometric analysis, remeshing, meshless methods, topology optimization, shape optimization, differentiable geometry, or AI-native mesh generation.
  • Experience with geometry repair, feature or simulation-intent recognition, parameterization, persistent correspondence, learning-based geometry representations, GPU spatial algorithms, or solver-aware adaptation.

title: DSX NVCRE Senior Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join our DSX team to build and operate the tooling that verifies AI infrastructure is ready for production. You will work on cluster readiness and certification software, including the open-source Cluster Readiness Engine, that validates GPU clusters across Kubernetes and Slurm, measures real training and inference performance, and produces evidence customers and partners can trust. We partner with the world's most innovative AI companies and cloud providers to make sure their infrastructure performs as designed before their most important workloads land on it.

What you will be doing:

  • Shape the Future of Validation. Design and build the systems that turn cluster validation from a manual exercise into repeatable, verifiable software. Your work will directly shape how NVIDIA and its partners qualify new GPU platforms and deployments.
  • Core Development. Design and implement cluster readiness and certification tooling in Go and Python that runs on Kubernetes and Slurm, including controllers, operators, CLIs, and scheduler integrations.
  • Benchmarking & Workloads. Build a catalog of benchmarks and real workloads spanning communication (NCCL), compute, storage, diagnostics, training, inference, reliability, and security, with per-architecture expectations and clear pass/fail criteria.
  • Data Provenance. Develop provenance and evidence pipelines that capture what actually ran, where it ran, and under which configuration, and that produce signed, auditable results.
  • Platform Integration. Bring new GPU platforms, schedulers, and fabrics under test, from first bring-up on a single node through multi-node validation on production clusters.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration.Collaborate with internal platform, networking, and solutions teams and with cloud partners to root-cause performance and correctness gaps found by the tooling, and feed fixes back into platforms and reference architectures.
  • Open Source Contribution. Contribute to the open-source Cluster Readiness Engine and related projects, including design documents, documentation, and reviews.
  • Technical Authorship. Author design documents, runbooks, and operational guides that codify how clusters are validated and how results are interpreted.

What we need to see:

  • BS, MS, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • 8+ years of software engineering experience building infrastructure or systems software, ideally for large-scale compute, cloud, or HPC environments.
  • Strong programming skills in Go and Python, with experience shipping production-quality services, controllers, or command-line tools.
  • Deep familiarity with Linux systems, containers, and Kubernetes, including writing operators or controllers against the Kubernetes API.
  • Working knowledge of HPC schedulers such as Slurm and of GPU cluster fundamentals: drivers, NCCL, InfiniBand or RoCE fabrics, and GPU health tooling such as DCGM.
  • Experience benchmarking or validating distributed systems, with a rigorous approach to measurement, reproducibility, and evidence.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive complex technical investigations to root cause and to communicate findings clearly to engineering and leadership audiences.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience running or tuning large-scale distributed training or inference workloads with frameworks such as PyTorch, Megatron, NeMo, vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.
  • Experience with the NVIDIA ecosystem, including DGX systems, GB200/GB300 platforms, CUDA, NVLink and NVSwitch fabrics, and NVIDIA networking.
  • Prior contributions to open-source infrastructure projects, especially Kubernetes operators, scheduler plugins, or benchmarking frameworks.
  • Background in software supply-chain security, attestation, or signed artifacts, and in building audit-grade evidence into systems.
  • Familiarity with observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry), GitOps workflows, and infrastructure as code for GPU clusters.

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer – Manufacturing & Supplier Engineering
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a hands-on Mechanical Engineer to be the local representative of our mechanical engineering team in Israel across our manufacturing sites and mechanical suppliers in China. You will be our mechanical expert on the ground, working directly with manufacturing partners and suppliers to address technical and manufacturing challenges and continuously improve the way our products are built. 

You will own manufacturing challenges from identification through implementation of the solution, support the design and improvement of jigs and fixtures, drive manufacturing process improvements, and help optimize production lines for quality, efficiency, and scalability. 

This role is ideal for a highly technical and creative engineer who enjoys working close to the hardware, tackling real-world manufacturing challenges, and thinking outside the box. You will act as a key bridge between our engineering teams in Israel and our manufacturing partners in China. 

NVIDIA Networking division is a leading supplier of innovative end-to-end InfiniBand and Ethernet connectivity solutions and services for servers and storage. We offer market-leading solutions that include adapter cards, switches, cables, and software to support networking technologies. Our products optimize data center performance and deliver industry-leading bandwidth and scalability. In addition, we serve a wide range of sectors including high-performance computing, enterprise, data centers, cloud computing and Web 2.0. We are constantly reinventing ourselves to stay ahead of the market and bring groundbreaking products and services to the industry. Our product line is focused on delivering the most optimized Ethernet and optical solutions for industries that can benefit from accelerated networking at scale. 


What you'll be doing: 

  • Acting as the on-site mechanical point of contact representing NVIDIA Israel's mechanical department across manufacturing sites and mechanical suppliers in China, owning the daily mechanical agenda across active programs. 
  • Working closely with manufacturing partners and mechanical part suppliers to investigate and address mechanical and manufacturing challenges, including quality and yield-related topics. 
  • Investigating manufacturing challenges, escalations and yield blockers on the production floor, applying structured root-cause methods such as fishbone and fault-tree analysis, with documented corrective actions. 
  • Supporting the design, development, troubleshooting and improvement of manufacturing jigs and fixtures, working directly with suppliers and production teams to implement practical solutions on the line. 
  • Driving manufacturing process improvements and production-line optimization, identifying opportunities to improve quality, efficiency, repeatability and scalability. 
  • Leading technical investigations on builds, line returns and qualification samples, including inspection, microscopy, dimensional metrology, cross-section, contamination and assembly-process analysis. 
  • Planning and running mechanical experiments and structured design-of-experiments on-site, aligning test plans with the Israel team, executing on the production floor, and reporting results back. 
  • Supporting bring-ups, pilot runs, production builds and mass production, with hands-on presence on the manufacturing floor to make real-time mechanical decisions and capture build learnings. 

What we need to see: 

  • Engineering diploma in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent experience. 
  • 8+ years of hands-on experience as a mechanical engineer in similar roles, such as datacom, server, networking, datacenter, or comparably complex electronic hardware products. 
  • Hands-on experience working with contract manufacturers, original design manufacturers, and/or mechanical part suppliers in new product introduction, ramp or mass-production environments. 
  • Strong technical capabilities and the ability to independently investigate and address complex mechanical and manufacturing challenges. 
  • Track record leading technical investigations from initial findings through verified root cause and implementation of documented corrective actions. 
  • Experience with manufacturing processes, production tooling, jigs and fixtures, including troubleshooting and improving existing manufacturing solutions. 
  • Hands-on knowledge and experience with joining and brazing processes, including high-frequency brazing, oven brazing, soldering, welding, and related manufacturing processes. 
  • Strong command of mechanical inspection and metrology, including geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, coordinate measuring machines, vision systems, gauges and dimensional analysis. 

Ways to stand out from the crowd: 

  • Prior on-site experience at a major contract manufacturer, ODM, or mechanical supplier in China or elsewhere in Asia. 
  • Strong knowledge of mechanical manufacturing processes and experience working directly with part suppliers. 
  • Experience designing, developing or improving manufacturing jigs, fixtures and production tooling. 
  • Strong practical experience in brazing, soldering and welding processes, including process development, qualification and manufacturing troubleshooting. 
  • Experience working in cleanroom environments.

title: Principal Engineer - Data Retrieval
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking an engineering lead to architect and scale the data acquisition infrastructure that powers our foundation models. Starting with code and STEM data for Nemotron, you will build the systems that discover valuable sources, crawl the open web at scale, and deliver reliable, high-quality data to training pipelines. This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning distributed systems, crawl infrastructure, and third-party data ingestion. You will own the architecture of a unified platform covering source discovery, URL indexing, crawl frontiers, predictive ranking, scheduling, distributed fetching, and ingestion. We have existing infrastructure to build on, and the goal is to bring it to pretraining scale and extend it to additional model families, modalities, and acquisition workflows over time. Along the way, you will lead architecture reviews and critical implementation work, mentor engineers, and help build the team.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Work with storage and scaling teams to design scalable frontier storage and queueing systems with high-throughput writes, efficient lookups, deduplication, and scheduling based on data quality, diversity, and freshness. Build a continuous discovery loop that extracts links and feeds new candidates back into the crawl frontier.
  • Develop a shared crawl execution layer that fetches reliably and politely at scale, handling dynamic websites while keeping resource use under control.
  • Build extensible pipelines for open-web, licensed, and partner content, including text, PDFs, code repositories, and multimodal assets. Define stable interfaces for source connectors so teams can add sources without rebuilding the platform.
  • Partner with parsing and curation teams to preserve valuable code, math, and structured content, and improve accepted data yield.
  • Implement provenance and policy enforcement with legal, privacy, security, and data governance partners. Translate approved publisher preferences, opt-outs, licensing terms, and use restrictions into auditable controls that follow the data downstream.
  • Own production readiness, including capacity planning, observability, fault tolerance, recovery, and cost efficiency. Instrument the pipeline end to end and set service objectives for throughput, freshness, reliability, and meeting training cutoffs.
  • Work with research and product teams to evaluate internal crawls and external datasets through comparable pilots. Deliver reproducible data releases that tie source coverage and processing quality to controlled training experiments.
  • Coordinate dependencies across teams and make clear tradeoffs between immediate data delivery and long-term platform development.

What we need to see:

  • A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • 15+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, including designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, setting technical direction, and delivering complex infrastructure across multiple teams.
  • Deep experience with web crawling or closely related discovery, indexing, or ingestion infrastructure, including distributed scheduling, stateful services, storage, and high-throughput data processing.
  • Strong hands-on engineering and system design skills. Ability to move between architecture, implementation, performance analysis, and production debugging.
  • Experience building batch or streaming pipelines and reasoning about consistency, retries, duplicate processing, backpressure, and recovery. A track record of improving throughput, latency, resource efficiency, or operational reliability.
  • Experience delivering data platforms for research, ML, search, or other demanding technical users. Ability to translate evolving requirements into clear interfaces and measurable engineering outcomes.
  • Strong technical communication and leadership through influence across engineering, product, research, and governance teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience architecting a web-wide crawl platform, scaling crawl frontier storage, or consolidating multiple acquisition systems into shared infrastructure.
  • Direct experience supplying foundation-model pretraining data, including targeted discovery, quality-aware crawl ranking, and acquisition of code or technical content.
  • Experience implementing publisher consent, training-use opt-outs, dataset licensing controls, or provenance infrastructure at scale.
  • Background with browser-based or agentic data collection, programmable extraction, and sandboxed environments for tool-use data or post-training evaluation.
  • Experience onboarding licensed or multimodal datasets, building reusable partner integrations, or delivering streaming feeds with low latency for retrieval and grounding.

The platform is a core capability for NVIDIA’s AI models and directly shapes the reach and quality of our training data. If you enjoy solving difficult distributed systems problems and building platforms that other teams depend on, we want to hear from you.

title: Cyber Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:

  • Build and refine detections and defense strategies based on threat models and attacker behaviors across cloud, identity, endpoint, and product telemetry, using frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK to map adversary tactics and enhance detection coverage.

title: SCG ArchDesign Engineer - New College Grad 2027
descriptionHtml:
Silicon Co-Design Group (SCG) is a wide-ranging, multi-functional, integral team at NVIDIA. We sit at the crossroads of design, architecture, marketing, operations, and productization. Our contributions span from the arch stage and extend to defining final products. We architect innovative solutions for Datacenter, Server, Gaming, Robotics, Automotive, and Embedded markets. We do all of this with an eye on making groundbreaking, impactful market disruptions! We are looking for a ArchDesign Co-Design Engineer(NCG),who approaches silicon co-design through prototyping and design of experiments: we build the vehicles, measurement plans, and analyses that show how power, performance, noise, circuit margin, and binning actually behave, then turn those results into tools and data pipelines that architecture, firmware, and manufacturing can use. This is a highly visible, multi-functional role. Success in this role requires owning silicon truth on messy bring-up and data: deciding what an experiment proved, catching when a number or a model is wrong, and leaving behind reusable methods other teams can ship against.

What you will be doing:

  • Standing up silicon co-design prototypes and measurement setups that expose power-rail noise, circuit margin, performance, and binning behavior — from first bring-up through a repeatable experiment others can rerun.
  • Planning and executing design of experiments (DOE): choosing factors and ranges (voltage, frequency, workload, temperature, process), defining sample plans and success criteria, and analyzing main effects and interactions so results are usable, not just collected.
  • Building Python pipelines and analyses that turn prototype, DOE, simulation, and characterization data (power, noise, Vmin/Fmax, binning yield) into traces, summaries, and inputs for firmware tuning, product specs, and manufacturing limits — with checks for schema, units, corners, and SKU mapping.
  • Partnering with architecture, design, validation, and firmware to add debug hooks, iterate the prototype, and document what the experiment proved versus what still needs silicon.
  • Using secure, traceable, validated AI-assisted workflows for experiment planning, analysis, and documentation, with human oversight on any conclusion that could affect limits, bins, or specs.

What we need to see:

  • MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 2+ years in a related silicon, validation, characterization, productization, or engineering-tools role (SoC, GPU, CPU, or similar).
  • Working knowledge of silicon speed/power/quality concepts — for example DVFS, Vmin/Fmax, shmoo, PDN/noise, binning, or guardband — and comfort learning DOE and prototype bring-up in a co-design setting.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of: lab or post-silicon bring-up, experiment or characterization campaigns, manufacturing test/limits, or tools/pipelines that consume chip data.
  • Proficiency in Python (or similar) for data analysis, automation, and validation; comfort with Git and structured test/regression. SQL or lightweight dashboards are a plus.
  • Ability to turn an ambiguous silicon question into a measurable experiment, communicate clearly across teams, and write notes others can execute from.
  • Strong AI-enabled skills and thinking — use AI to accelerate analysis, exploration, and documentation while maintaining rigor, originality, and judgment that do not come from AI.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • You have run a test-chip, prototype vehicle, or characterization DOE and can explain what you would change in the next matrix.
  • Direct experience on GPU/SoC/CPU power, performance, binning, PDN/noise, or sim-to-silicon correlation.
  • You have shipped an internal tool, dashboard, or data pipeline (Python, databases, web apps) that other people actually use.
  • Hands-on LLMs in an engineering workflow — agents, RAG, or evaluation — including a time you had to debug a wrong or unsafe answer.
  • Exposure to firmware/BIOS parameters, eFuse/limits, or ATE/SLT screening, and how they connect to product SKUs.

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered one of the world's most desirable technology employers. We welcome you to join our team, which consists of some of the hardest-working people in the world, working together to promote rapid growth. Are you passionate about joining a best-in-class team supporting the latest in GPU and AI technology? If so, we want to hear from you.

title: AI Compiler and Kernel Intern – Summer 2027
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is looking for an AI Compiler & Kernel Intern to apply AI agents, machine learning, and performance engineering to compilers, GPU kernels, and developer tools. You will work with compiler, kernel, and AI engineers on a scoped project involving code, compiler and kernel feedback, performance experiments, and optimization. Depending on your background and interests, the work may focus on agentic workflows, learned models, compiler optimization, GPU kernel development, performance analysis, or AI-enabled developer tools. Candidates may enter from either a compiler or kernel background; experience in every area is not expected.


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Build AI-agent workflows that interact with code, compilers, GPU kernels, benchmarks, performance tools, and engineering systems.
  • Develop tools that help agents collect data, run experiments, analyze compiler, kernel, and performance feedback, identify optimization opportunities, and recommend next steps.
  • Explore data-driven approaches for compiler optimization, GPU kernel generation and tuning, performance prediction, decision support, and workflow automation.
  • Build reliable interfaces between AI agents and compiler, kernel, or developer-tool infrastructure.
  • Prototype improvements to compiler flows, code generation, GPU kernels, optimization tools, experimentation systems, or developer workflows.
  • Work with compiler, kernel, architecture, AI, and performance engineers to evaluate ideas on representative workloads.
  • Measure correctness, runtime performance, compile time, resource utilization, reliability, and other relevant outcomes.
  • Document the design, experiments, results, limitations, and next steps.


What We Need to See:

  • Pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a similar field.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, C, C++, or a similar language.
  • Solid foundations in data structures, algorithms, software engineering, and quantitative problem solving.
  • Coursework, research, or project experience in one or more of these areas: AI, machine learning, AI agents, compilers, programming languages, GPU kernels, CUDA or accelerator programming, systems, performance engineering, optimization, or developer tools.
  • Ability to design experiments, analyze results, investigate technical problems, and communicate findings clearly.
  • Experience working in one or more of AI, compiler, kernel, performance, or systems areas, with the ability to learn across technical boundaries.


Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Experience building AI agents, LLM applications, evaluation systems, coding workflows, or developer tools.
  • Experience with LLVM, MLIR, compiler optimization passes, code generation, domain-specific languages, or compiler infrastructure.
  • Experience writing, analyzing, or optimizing GPU kernels using CUDA, Triton, or a similar accelerator programming model.
  • Hands-on experience with reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, predictive modeling, ranking, search, or high-dimensional data analysis.

Research, internships, open-source contributions, or personal projects that measure runtime, compile time, resource use, code quality, or developer productivity

Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 20 USD – 94 USD.

You will also be eligible for Intern benefits. ​

title: Senior Vision Language Model Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is the platform upon which every new AI-powered application is built. We are seeking a senior vision language model engineer to design and build agentic data and training workflows for Autonomous Vehicles, Robotics, and Medical applications. The right person for this role brings technical innovation and collaborative culture to change the way NVIDIA builds dataset search platforms for physical AI developers. Our dataset search offerings are ease to use, performant and scalable. Your work will redefine the dataset search and model training capabilities in NVIDIA product offerings and impact the most iconic companies in Physical AI.


What you'll be doing:

  • Partner with our researchers to develop and evaluate prototypes of our latest models, such as VLMs and VLAs, for video search, video understanding, and more. Enable fundamental advances in autonomous driving, healthcare, and robotics.
  • Design and implement agentic data workflows that automate data discovery, labeling, evaluation, and retraining to maximize development velocity.
  • Build, curate, and maintain high‑quality multimodal datasets (e.g., video, sensor, language/action traces) tailored for end‑to‑end physical AI problems, such as autonomous driving.
  • Explore and productize new data sources including simulation and synthetic data.
  • Use agentic AI workflows across the full applied research lifecycle.
  • Collaborate with research, model development, performance, and product teams.
  • Contribute to NVIDIA Cosmos Dataset Search and other core NVIDIA platforms and products.

What we need to see:

  • PhD with 4+ years, MS with 6+ years, or BS (or equivalent experience) with 8+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field
  • Strong background in modern deep learning, including transformer‑based architectures, video modeling, and multimodal VLM/VLA or foundation models.
  • Excellent experience training and deploying deep learning models on real‑world datasets: data preprocessing, distributed training, evaluation, debugging, and iterative improvement.
  • Excellent experience with python and at least one deep learning framework.
  • Current with the latest research on image and video search in autonomous vehicles, healthcare, robotics, or related physical AI applications.
  • Fluent with agentic AI workflows across the full applied research lifecycle, including prototyping novel algorithms and search pipelines, benchmarking, and integrating prototypes in production codebases.
  • Clear and effective communication skills, with experience working well in a dynamic, product- and research-focused team.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Strong track record publishing in top-tier conference such as CVPR, NeuRIPS, ICML, ECCV
  • Patents in video retrieval or related field
  • Strong coding architecture skills demonstrated through contributions to large internal or open-source projects.
  • Experience in robotic systems such as autonomous vehicles or humanoid robotics.

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package (www.nvidiabenefits.com ), we are widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our best-in-class engineering teams are rapidly growing. If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with a real passion for technology, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Networking Architect
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA Networking has been a leader in high performance networking infrastructure for many years. The next unit of computing is the datacenter, and the network makes it all possible. NVIDIA is looking to grow its networking architecture team with people passionate about accelerated computing. We are looking for you, a Senior Networking Architect, to develop the next generation of network for AI. If you love researching new technologies, we'd love to hear from you!

What you’ll be doing:

  • The position includes an active part in research and development of networking solutions to enable the next generation of accelerated data centers.

  • The position spans over various layers from ASIC design to algorithms, topologies and systems, and more.

  • Partner with internal teams, strategic partners, standard bodies and networking communities to initiate and develop groundbreaking networking solutions for AI!

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc or M.Sc degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience

  • 5+ years of previous industry or research experience in computer networks

  • Experience in developing ASICs and/or real-time software running on the ASICs

  • Proven understanding in networking and routing protocols, and their implementations

  • Strong problem-solving and critical thinking skills

  • Works and operates in a highly dynamic and multifaceted environment

  • Ability to work concurrently with multiple groups in the organization and with strategic partners

Ways to stand out of the crowd:

  • Deep knowledge in RDMA, with focus on RoCE

  • Understanding of various network topologies and their attributes

  • Understanding and experience with load balancing and congestion control algorithms

  • Proven practice of industry standards and/or the experience of working with standards organizations and/or open source communities

  • Strong skills with Python and/or C++

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers.
